points.quote: Using digital tools including AI to help you with things like editing and refining your writing (spelling, grammar, syntax, and clarity ) is permissible and does not require attribution.
points.gist: Using AI or digital tools to edit and refine writing (spelling, grammar, syntax, clarity) is permitted and needs no attribution.

points.quote: However, where AI is used to create content that forms part of an assessment this must be attributed as detailed above in the section on plagiarism.
points.gist: Where AI is used to create content forming part of an assessment, that use must be attributed.

points.quote: Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications to create work or elements of work without fully attributing their use.
points.gist: Listed as plagiarism: using AI applications to create work or elements of work without fully attributing their use.

points.quote: use AI to support and assist – not replace – your own voice and ideas.
points.gist: Study Skills Hub guidance: use AI to support and assist, not replace, your own voice and ideas.

points.quote: Deliberately presenting outputs from AI applications as your work (false authorship) .
points.anchor: Examples of Academic Misconduct in Each Category: Gross Academic Misconduct
points.gist: Deliberately presenting AI outputs as your own work (false authorship) is listed as gross academic misconduct.

points.quote: Presenting work that has been processed through AI applications beyond that permitted by the third -party proofreading and editing guidelines referenced above .
points.anchor: Examples of Academic Misconduct in Each Category: Major Academic Misconduct
points.gist: Presenting work processed through AI beyond what the proofreading and editing guidelines permit is listed as major academic misconduct.

points.quote: Minimal use of AI to generate content without acknowledging the source.
points.anchor: Examples of Academic Misconduct in Each Category: Minor Academic Misconduct
points.gist: Minimal use of AI to generate content without acknowledgement is listed as minor academic misconduct.

points.quote: Failing to attribute the use of AI applications in generating elements of audio -visual content.
points.anchor: Examples of Academic Misconduct in Each Category: Major Academic Misconduct
points.gist: Failing to attribute AI use in generating elements of audio-visual content is listed as major academic misconduct.

points.quote: Fail Course no right to retrieve credit or progress.
points.gist: The penalties table lists failing the course, with no right to retrieve credit or progress, as a penalty.

points.quote: references must be submitted in Harvard form at, citing any cover songs performed
points.gist: References must be submitted in Harvard format, citing any cover songs performed.

points.quote: provided it does not comprise more than 20% of the total volume and is appropriately referenced or used in appendices or supplementary materials.
points.gist: Previously submitted work may be used in a dissertation or final-year project if under 20% of total volume and referenced or appended.

points.quote: You must make it clear whenever you work collaboratively and name all those who collaborated
points.gist: Students must make clear when they work collaboratively and name everyone who collaborated.

points.quote: Where a student fails to attend or make alternative arrangements, the investigation should proceed , and consideration should be given to the available evidence .
points.anchor: Suspected Major or Gross Academic Misconduct
points.gist: If a student neither attends the interview nor makes alternative arrangements, the investigation proceeds on the available evidence.

points.quote: the total time to complete a major or gross academic misconduct case is normally 25 working days.
points.anchor: Suspected Major or Gross Academic Misconduct
points.gist: The total time to complete a major or gross misconduct case is normally 25 working days.

points.quote: Appeals against academic misconduct decisions are considered in the same way as an academic appeal, under the Student Appeals Procedure .
points.anchor: Appeals Against Decisions on Academic Misconduct
points.gist: Appeals against misconduct decisions are handled like an academic appeal, under the Student Appeals Procedure.
